welcome.title: MARS+ · plan a Mars EVA
welcome.what: You are in the habitat at Octavia E. Butler Landing (Jezero crater). Your crew wants to walk ~900 m to the Issole outcrop to document signs of ancient water and take a sample — safely.
welcome.step1: Read the verdict at the top: GO or NO-GO, which plan and when to leave.
welcome.step2: Change the conditions — weather scenario, dust or solar alerts, time limit, pace — and see why each plan passes or fails.
welcome.step3: Plan your own route: press “Set A” and “Set B” and click the map. The least-effort path is computed in your browser.
welcome.data: Built with NASA data: HiRISE terrain and imagery, Perseverance weather (MEDA) and photos, Curiosity radiation (RAD).
summary.noGo: No plan is safe under the current conditions — postpone the EVA.

mission.title: Mission
mission.lead: Walk from Octavia E. Butler Landing to the Issole outcrop, document signs of water alteration, collect a sample and return safely.
mission.note: Times at normal pace. Sand doubles walking time; ~520 m of large dunes surround Issole and cannot be avoided. The straight line would cross blocked rocky cells.
route.title: Plan your own route (A → B)
route.help: Press “Set A”, click the map, then “Set B” and click again. With the keyboard: focus the map, move it with the arrow keys and press Enter to drop the point at the crosshair. The least-effort route is computed in your browser over the 2 m terrain grid of the pilot area.

plans.title: EVA plan
plans.lead: Every plan is tested at every departure hour through five filters: terrain → science → time → weather → radiation. A plan that fails one filter is out; nothing compensates for a safety failure.
plans.dustBackgroundValue: Jezero τ880 = {tau} (median of sols {from}–{to}, storm sols left out). The alert turns on at τ ≥ {threshold}. Worst weather uses the same dust: worst means temperature and wind.
plans.dustStormValue: Jezero τ880 = {tau} (highest daily median on sols {from}–{to}). The alert turns on at τ ≥ {threshold}. Sol 313 has no Mastcam-Z tau in this table.
plans.dustSolValue: Jezero τ880 = {tau} on sol {sol} (Ls {ls}°, {n} images). The alert turns on at τ ≥ {threshold}.
plans.dustMissing: No Mastcam-Z τ880 on sol {sol}. The alert stays off unless you turn it on. Threshold τ ≥ {threshold}.
plans.dustUnavailable: No dust measurement is loaded. Threshold τ ≥ {threshold}. The alert stays off unless you turn it on.
explain.recommended: Recommended: Plan {planId} — {planName}. Depart {departure}, back {returnTime} ({totalMin} min, {dose} µGy).
explain.departureWindow: Plan {planId} works for departures from {from} to {to}.
explain.postpone: Postpone the EVA. Closest option: Plan {planId} at {departure} — {filterName}: {reason}.
explain.filterCounts: {viable} of {total} candidates are viable. Rejected by terrain {c1}, science {c2}, time {c3}, weather {c4}, radiation {c5}.

weather.title: Weather at Issole (MEDA)
weather.lead: Ground temperature and wind measured by Perseverance while it was at Issole (sols 286–339). The shaded band is the recommended EVA.
weather.note: Ground temperature derived from TIRS infrared irradiance (emissivity 0.99). Midday gusts reached 17–19 m/s. Dust opacity is not in those derived MEDA files. The alert uses Mastcam-Z 880 nm optical depth (Lemmon, CC BY 4.0). The table is marked preliminary. Lemmon et al. 2022 also report an RDS visible peak near 1.7 during the storm; that peak is not a row in the table.
radiation.title: Radiation (RAD, October 2021)
radiation.lead: Surface dose rate measured by Curiosity's RAD before, during and after the 28 Oct 2021 solar particle event — the first ground-level event recorded on Earth, the Moon and Mars.
radiation.eva: Recommended EVA: {dose} µGy over {outsideMin} min outside ({share}% of a surface day).
radiation.noEva: No EVA recommended under the current conditions.
radiation.note: Absorbed dose (µGy), RAD detector E, Gale crater. Jezero sits higher than Gale, with less atmosphere overhead, so the local dose would be somewhat larger. Cosmic rays are uniform at this scale: less time outside means less dose.
geology.title: Geology & science target
geology.lead: Units from the Mars 2020 Science Team photogeologic map (Stack et al. 2020), aligned with the HiRISE terrain.
geology.target: Science target: Issole is an olivine-rich igneous rock with carbonates and hydrated sulfates — evidence that water altered it after it formed. Perseverance cored Robine (sol 298) and Malay (sol 337) here.
assumptions.title: Assumptions & limits
assumptions.rocks: Rocks: {rocks}. Rocks smaller than ~0.75 m are invisible from orbit. Checked against Perseverance's real drive (see Mission).
assumptions.eva: EVA budget: airlock {airlock} min + reserve {reserve} min; tasks: photo {photo} min, sample {sample} min.
assumptions.weather: Weather thresholds: ground ≥ {minC} °C and mean wind ≤ {maxMs} m/s for every hour outside.
assumptions.dust: Dust: the EVA is postponed when Mastcam-Z 880 nm optical depth is at least {tau}. The Issole background median is about 0.50 (every non-storm day under 0.85) and the measured storm peak is 1.38 on sols 316–317. Orbital dust maps are hundreds of kilometres across and do not separate the routes.
assumptions.stops: Stops: the flattest rock-free workspace near the rover positions for Robine and Malay (slope ≤ {slope}°, large-dune fraction ≤ {dune}; the rover arm works ~2 m ahead of the rover).
assumptions.whole: Plans are checked as a whole. The only change mid-route is the emergency return to the habitat; choosing new stops mid-route is out of scope for this pilot.

sens.title: Sand sensitivity
sens.lead: How much does the result depend on the sand assumption? Routes and plans are recomputed in your browser with walking time on large dunes ×1.5, ×2 (model) and ×3.
sens.error: The sensitivity test could not run.
sens.stable: Robust: the recommended plan and departure do not change with the sand assumption.
sens.changes: The recommendation depends on the sand assumption — treat it with caution.
rover.compare: Perseverance drove {dist} m to reach Issole ({ratio}× our route): rover wheels must avoid dunes where they can get stuck, and it visited other science targets on the way. Astronauts can cross sand with extra effort, which the model charges for.
validation.text: Validation: along the ~{len} m that Perseverance actually drove inside this area, the model blocks only {pct}% of the cells ({cells} of {total}; area average {area}%). Terrain known to be passable is not flagged as an obstacle.

emergency.title: Emergency return
emergency.lead: A dust storm or a solar particle event cannot be dodged inside this area: dust covers hundreds of km and particles come from the whole sky. If an alert arrives during the walk, the answer is the best way back to the habitat. It is prepared before leaving and used by the person in the habitat, who guides the crew by radio.

emergency.dust: Dust storm (low visibility: safest way back)

emergency.whyDust: Dust-safe route: no slopes above the dust limit, avoids large dunes where it can and keeps the habitat in view, walked slower for low visibility. Dose rate {rate} µGy/h; {dunes} m of large dunes.
emergency.vsFast: Against the fastest route at the same pace: +{min} min and +{dose} µGy, {dunes} m less of large dunes.

emergency.tableTitle: Return time from each stop, prepared before leaving
emergency.assumption: Scenario assumptions (config/model-parameters.json → contingency): the position is estimated from progress along the planned route (Mars has no GPS); the habitat is the only shelter; how much warning an alert gives on Mars is not modelled.

assumptions.emergency: Emergency return: fastest route for a solar particle event (dose at {rate} µGy/h, the peak of 28 Oct 2021); dust-safe route for a storm (slope ≤ {slope}°, large dunes and cells without view of the habitat avoided where possible, walked ×{pace} slower). Warning above {max} min from the habitat. Scenario assumptions pending the science team.

gravity.title: Mars gravity
gravity.lead: On Mars everything weighs {pct}% of its Earth weight (3.71 m/s²). What that changes for a walk:
gravity.weight: Loads: suit, tools and samples weigh {pct}% of their Earth weight but keep all their mass: they are just as hard to start, stop and turn.
gravity.speed: Speed: people switch from walking to running sooner in low gravity, at about {mars} km/h on Mars against {earth} km/h on Earth. The model’s suited pace ({model} km/h on flat ground) stays well below that limit.
gravity.slopes: Slopes: climbing costs less energy, but grip also falls with gravity, so descents on loose sand slip more easily. That is why slopes above the block limit stay forbidden.
gravity.falls: Falls: falling 1 m takes {mars} s on Mars against {earth} s on Earth: more time to react and a slower impact.
gravity.calcOut: {kg} kg on Mars weighs like {eq} kg on Earth.
gravity.model: This explains the model; it does not change the walking-cost formula (the suited pace is a scenario assumption).
